Here are simple, safe ways to add more walking to your day:

• **Start small:** Walk 5–10 minutes at a time. Add 2–5 minutes each week only if it feels comfortable.  
• **Walk after meals:** A gentle 5–10 minute stroll after breakfast, lunch, or dinner builds a routine and aids digestion.  
• **Use work breaks:** Stand up, stretch, and walk around your office, down a hallway, or outside for 3–5 minutes every hour.  
• **Tweak daily habits:** Park farther from entrances, get off the bus/train one stop early, or walk to a nearby mailbox instead of driving.  
• **Pair with something you already do:** Walk while on phone calls, listening to music, or watching a TV show.  
• **Wear proper shoes:** Choose comfortable, supportive walking shoes with good grip. Dress in light layers for the weather.  
• **Track simply:** Use a basic pedometer, phone step counter, or just write down your daily minutes. Consistency matters more than numbers.  
• **Listen to your body:** Stop if you feel joint pain, dizziness, chest discomfort, or unusual breathlessness. Rest and adjust as needed.  
• **Check with your doctor first:** Especially if you have heart conditions, balance concerns, or joint issues, a quick check-in ensures it’s safe to start.

**Key takeaway:** You don’t need long or fast walks. Spreading 15–20 minutes of gentle walking across your day is enough to build the habit safely and sustainably.
